# build step ordering

A release tool plans the order of build steps from a flat list of `name:dependencies` entries and must produce byte-identical plans on every platform.

This repository holds the Go implementation (`planorder.go`). It is being ported to Rust; the port must behave exactly like the specification below, including for malformed input.

## Behaviour

A build tool plans the order of steps. A step is a string `name:dep1,dep2` (a step without dependencies is `name:` or just
`name`). Names and dependency names match `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]*`. The same dependency may be listed twice (it counts once). It is an
error if a step name appears twice, a name or dependency is malformed (including an empty item such as `a:b,` or `a:,b`), a
dependency is not the name of any step, or the steps contain a dependency **cycle** (a step that depends on itself counts).

* `build_order(steps)`: all step names, every step after its dependencies; whenever several steps are ready, the one with
  the **smallest name** (plain character order) is taken first.
* `layers(steps)`: layer `k` holds the steps whose longest dependency chain has length `k` (layer 0 has no dependencies);
  every layer is sorted by name; there are no empty layers. No steps gives no layers.
* `blockers(steps, name)`: the names of all steps `name` depends on, directly or indirectly, sorted; unknown `name` is an error.
* `ready_after(steps, done)`: the steps not in `done` whose dependencies are all in `done`, sorted. `done` may repeat a name;
  a name in `done` that is not a step is an error.

## Functions

* `build_order(steps)` -> `list<str>`. Fails on invalid input. (`steps`: list<str>)
* `layers(steps)` -> `list<list<str>>`. Fails on invalid input. (`steps`: list<str>)
* `blockers(steps, name)` -> `list<str>`. Fails on invalid input. (`steps`: list<str>, `name`: str)
* `ready_after(steps, done)` -> `list<str>`. Fails on invalid input. (`steps`: list<str>, `done`: list<str>)

Types: `str` is Unicode text; `list<T>` is an ordered sequence.

## Go (source)

```go
func BuildOrder(steps []string) ([]string, error)
func Layers(steps []string) ([][]string, error)
func Blockers(steps []string, name string) ([]string, error)
func ReadyAfter(steps []string, done []string) ([]string, error)
```

## Rust (target)

Create `src/lib.rs` (and any extra files you need).

Crate `plan_order`: everything is reachable from `src/lib.rs` (extra modules are fine; re-export them). Failure is an `Err(_)` (the error type is yours); never panic on bad input. No dependencies.

```rust
pub fn build_order(steps: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<String>, E>
pub fn layers(steps: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<Vec<String>>, E>
pub fn blockers(steps: &[String], name: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, E>
pub fn ready_after(steps: &[String], done: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<String>, E>
```

## Checking

`tests/vectors.rs` reads the vector file `vectors/examples.json` (a small sample) and calls the Rust API; run `cargo test --offline`. The same harness is used with a much larger vector file when the port is graded, so passing the examples only is not enough. The harness files and `vectors/examples.json` must not be edited.

# build step ordering

A release tool plans the order of build steps from a flat list of `name:dependencies` entries and must produce byte-identical plans on every platform.

This repository holds the Rust implementation (`src/lib.rs`). It is being ported to Python; the port must behave exactly like the specification below, including for malformed input.

## Behaviour

A build tool plans the order of steps. A step is a string `name:dep1,dep2` (a step without dependencies is `name:` or just
`name`). Names and dependency names match `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]*`. The same dependency may be listed twice (it counts once). It is an
error if a step name appears twice, a name or dependency is malformed (including an empty item such as `a:b,` or `a:,b`), a
dependency is not the name of any step, or the steps contain a dependency **cycle** (a step that depends on itself counts).

* `build_order(steps)`: all step names, every step after its dependencies; whenever several steps are ready, the one with
  the **smallest name** (plain character order) is taken first.
* `layers(steps)`: layer `k` holds the steps whose longest dependency chain has length `k` (layer 0 has no dependencies);
  every layer is sorted by name; there are no empty layers. No steps gives no layers.
* `blockers(steps, name)`: the names of all steps `name` depends on, directly or indirectly, sorted; unknown `name` is an error.
* `ready_after(steps, done)`: the steps not in `done` whose dependencies are all in `done`, sorted. `done` may repeat a name;
  a name in `done` that is not a step is an error.

## Functions

* `build_order(steps)` -> `list<str>`. Fails on invalid input. (`steps`: list<str>)
* `layers(steps)` -> `list<list<str>>`. Fails on invalid input. (`steps`: list<str>)
* `blockers(steps, name)` -> `list<str>`. Fails on invalid input. (`steps`: list<str>, `name`: str)
* `ready_after(steps, done)` -> `list<str>`. Fails on invalid input. (`steps`: list<str>, `done`: list<str>)

Types: `str` is Unicode text; `list<T>` is an ordered sequence.

## Rust (source)

```rust
pub fn build_order(steps: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<String>, E>
pub fn layers(steps: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<Vec<String>>, E>
pub fn blockers(steps: &[String], name: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, E>
pub fn ready_after(steps: &[String], done: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<String>, E>
```

## Python (target)

Create `plan_order.py` (and any extra files you need).

Module `plan_order` (file `plan_order.py` at the repository root). Plain `int`/`str`/`list` values. Failure is signalled by raising an exception (any subclass of `Exception`).

```python
def build_order(steps: list[str]) -> list[str]
def layers(steps: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]
def blockers(steps: list[str], name: str) -> list[str]
def ready_after(steps: list[str], done: list[str]) -> list[str]
```

## Checking

`tests/test_vectors.py` reads the vector file `vectors/examples.json` (a small sample) and calls the Python API; run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`. The same harness is used with a much larger vector file when the port is graded, so passing the examples only is not enough. The harness files and `vectors/examples.json` must not be edited.

# build step ordering

A release tool plans the order of build steps from a flat list of `name:dependencies` entries and must produce byte-identical plans on every platform.

This repository holds the Python implementation (`plan_order.py`). It is being ported to Go; the port must behave exactly like the specification below, including for malformed input.

## Behaviour

A build tool plans the order of steps. A step is a string `name:dep1,dep2` (a step without dependencies is `name:` or just
`name`). Names and dependency names match `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]*`. The same dependency may be listed twice (it counts once). It is an
error if a step name appears twice, a name or dependency is malformed (including an empty item such as `a:b,` or `a:,b`), a
dependency is not the name of any step, or the steps contain a dependency **cycle** (a step that depends on itself counts).

* `build_order(steps)`: all step names, every step after its dependencies; whenever several steps are ready, the one with
  the **smallest name** (plain character order) is taken first.
* `layers(steps)`: layer `k` holds the steps whose longest dependency chain has length `k` (layer 0 has no dependencies);
  every layer is sorted by name; there are no empty layers. No steps gives no layers.
* `blockers(steps, name)`: the names of all steps `name` depends on, directly or indirectly, sorted; unknown `name` is an error.
* `ready_after(steps, done)`: the steps not in `done` whose dependencies are all in `done`, sorted. `done` may repeat a name;
  a name in `done` that is not a step is an error.

## Functions

* `build_order(steps)` -> `list<str>`. Fails on invalid input. (`steps`: list<str>)
* `layers(steps)` -> `list<list<str>>`. Fails on invalid input. (`steps`: list<str>)
* `blockers(steps, name)` -> `list<str>`. Fails on invalid input. (`steps`: list<str>, `name`: str)
* `ready_after(steps, done)` -> `list<str>`. Fails on invalid input. (`steps`: list<str>, `done`: list<str>)

Types: `str` is Unicode text; `list<T>` is an ordered sequence.

## Python (source)

```python
def build_order(steps: list[str]) -> list[str]
def layers(steps: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]
def blockers(steps: list[str], name: str) -> list[str]
def ready_after(steps: list[str], done: list[str]) -> list[str]
```

## Go (target)

The Go API already exists as stubs (every function fails at run time); replace the bodies.

Package `planorder` in the repository root (module `example.com/planorder`, standard library only). Use the integer widths shown in the signatures. Failure is a non-nil `error` returned to the caller; never `panic` on bad input. A `(T, bool)` result reports whether a value is present.

```go
func BuildOrder(steps []string) ([]string, error)
func Layers(steps []string) ([][]string, error)
func Blockers(steps []string, name string) ([]string, error)
func ReadyAfter(steps []string, done []string) ([]string, error)
```

## Checking

`vectors_test.go` reads the vector file `vectors/examples.json` (a small sample) and calls the Go API; run `go test ./...`. The same harness is used with a much larger vector file when the port is graded, so passing the examples only is not enough. The harness files and `vectors/examples.json` must not be edited.

# build step ordering

A release tool plans the order of build steps from a flat list of `name:dependencies` entries and must produce byte-identical plans on every platform.

This repository holds the Go implementation (`planorder.go`). It is being ported to Python; the port must behave exactly like the specification below, including for malformed input.

## Behaviour

A build tool plans the order of steps. A step is a string `name:dep1,dep2` (a step without dependencies is `name:` or just
`name`). Names and dependency names match `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]*`. The same dependency may be listed twice (it counts once). It is an
error if a step name appears twice, a name or dependency is malformed (including an empty item such as `a:b,` or `a:,b`), a
dependency is not the name of any step, or the steps contain a dependency **cycle** (a step that depends on itself counts).

* `build_order(steps)`: all step names, every step after its dependencies; whenever several steps are ready, the one with
  the **smallest name** (plain character order) is taken first.
* `layers(steps)`: layer `k` holds the steps whose longest dependency chain has length `k` (layer 0 has no dependencies);
  every layer is sorted by name; there are no empty layers. No steps gives no layers.
* `blockers(steps, name)`: the names of all steps `name` depends on, directly or indirectly, sorted; unknown `name` is an error.
* `ready_after(steps, done)`: the steps not in `done` whose dependencies are all in `done`, sorted. `done` may repeat a name;
  a name in `done` that is not a step is an error.

## Functions

* `build_order(steps)` -> `list<str>`. Fails on invalid input. (`steps`: list<str>)
* `layers(steps)` -> `list<list<str>>`. Fails on invalid input. (`steps`: list<str>)
* `blockers(steps, name)` -> `list<str>`. Fails on invalid input. (`steps`: list<str>, `name`: str)
* `ready_after(steps, done)` -> `list<str>`. Fails on invalid input. (`steps`: list<str>, `done`: list<str>)

Types: `str` is Unicode text; `list<T>` is an ordered sequence.

## Go (source)

```go
func BuildOrder(steps []string) ([]string, error)
func Layers(steps []string) ([][]string, error)
func Blockers(steps []string, name string) ([]string, error)
func ReadyAfter(steps []string, done []string) ([]string, error)
```

## Python (target)

The Python API already exists as stubs (every function fails at run time); replace the bodies.

Module `plan_order` (file `plan_order.py` at the repository root). Plain `int`/`str`/`list` values. Failure is signalled by raising an exception (any subclass of `Exception`).

```python
def build_order(steps: list[str]) -> list[str]
def layers(steps: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]
def blockers(steps: list[str], name: str) -> list[str]
def ready_after(steps: list[str], done: list[str]) -> list[str]
```

## Checking

`tests/test_vectors.py` reads the vector file `vectors/examples.json` (a small sample) and calls the Python API; run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`. The same harness is used with a much larger vector file when the port is graded, so passing the examples only is not enough. The harness files and `vectors/examples.json` must not be edited.
